chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Photographs from Edward G. Robinson and Bessie Love at the Palace
summary: The only photos he has are autographed ones he asked for from Edward G. Robinson and Bessie Love when he worked the Palace Theatre in the Thirties.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: No, I never thought about getting together with them and having my picture taken, and this-that-and-the-other. The nearest I come to anything like that, I worked the Palace Theatre...oh, this is way back in the Thirties. Edward G. Robinson was on the bill and Kate Smith was on the bill, and Bessie Love -- Bessie Love was a movie star. Well, Edward G. Robinson at that time, he was just starting in pictures. He was a big man, he was a big star. So I went to Edward G. Robinson in his dressing room, and I asked him for a photograph. And he gave it to me. And I went into Bessie Love's room, and she gave one to me -- an autographed photograph.

But I mean, I had never did anything like that! And all down through my career I never did it no more. I got Edward G. Robinson's and Bessie Love's -- Kate Smith didn't have any photographs of herself. I didn't get none of her anyway, and I worked with her twice. I didn't ask her for one the second time. But Bessie Love I got. And I got 'em,
I still got 'em, and I cherish them.

But I worked with, oh, hundreds of big stars. Nothin' to prove it. Now, I worked with Louis for five years. I don't think there's a picture where I'm even shakin' hands with Louis or anything, just the two of us. Never. Nothin'. Same with Duke Ellington I have nothing to prove that I even know him. And so many of the others. Not to go that far back, but even... Well, anyway...
